title: The "Payment Screenshot" Ruse
learningObjectives: Verify credits directly in your own banking app rather than trusting buyer screenshots
Recognize fabricated time pressure designed to bypass verification checks
Maintain firm safety boundaries during in-person marketplace handovers
startingContext: You listed a scientific calculator on a campus student marketplace. Buyer Rohan K. claims he transferred ₹1,800 and sends a receipt screenshot, insisting his bus departs in 5 minutes.

redFlags.label: Payment screenshot presented as proof of payment
redFlags.explanation: Screenshots are easily altered or generated via fake receipt generator tools.

redFlags.label: Artificial time pressure
redFlags.explanation: Scammers claim buses are leaving or deadlines are looming to bypass balance checks.

redFlags.label: Payment receipt marked "Processing"
redFlags.explanation: Processing indicates money has not settled and may never be credited.

redFlags.label: Pressure to bypass checking own account balance
redFlags.explanation: Excuses about bank delays are used to guilt sellers into handing over goods.

messageOrEvent.speaker: Rohan K. (fictional)
messageOrEvent.text: Bhai, I just sent ₹1,800 to your UPI ID! Here is the payment screenshot. My bus leaves from campus gate in 5 minutes, please hand over the calculator quickly!

feedback.safeAlternative: Always check your own banking application for verified credit before parting with goods.
feedback.considerNext: Never rely on buyer devices or receipts when transferring merchandise.

choices.label: Hand it over — screenshot looks fine

explanation.whatHappened: You handed over the calculator relying solely on the buyer's screenshot.
explanation.why: Screenshots can be mocked easily; the funds never credited to your account.

choices.label: Check my own UPI app for the credit first

explanation.whatHappened: You paused and opened your own banking app to verify actual credit.
explanation.why: Only your own bank balance provides authoritative proof of an incoming transfer.

choices.label: Ask him to resend the screenshot

explanation.whatHappened: You asked for another screenshot instead of inspecting your own balance.
explanation.why: Requesting another screenshot wastes time and still relies on unverified sender claims.

messageOrEvent.speaker: Rohan K. (fictional)
messageOrEvent.text: Look, my bank server is slow today! I already showed you the debit slip. My bus is honking, are you calling me a liar? Just give it!

feedback.safeAlternative: Politely decline to release the item until your bank reflects the balance.
feedback.considerNext: Do not let social awkwardness or accusations override basic safety.

explanation.whatHappened: You yielded to emotional pressure and surrendered the item without verification.
explanation.why: Scammers deliberately feign irritation to make sellers feel guilty.

choices.label: Wait a few minutes, then check my own app

explanation.whatHappened: You insisted on waiting before verifying your account.
explanation.why: Waiting reduces urgency, though immediate account verification is safer.

choices.label: Handover only once money shows in my account

explanation.whatHappened: You set a firm rule that items are released only after money reflects.
explanation.why: Setting clear safety boundaries stops fake-payment scams instantly.

messageOrEvent.speaker: Your Bank App (fictional)
messageOrEvent.text: Account Balance: ₹320. No incoming credit of ₹1,800 found in transaction history. Buyer texts: 'Bank delay bro, trust me, give it!'

feedback.safeAlternative: Never complete transactions based on promises of delayed funds.
feedback.considerNext: Report suspicious buyers on student marketplace boards.

explanation.whatHappened: You ignored your bank app confirmation and trusted his promise.
explanation.why: Never hand over goods when your own bank confirms zero payment.

choices.label: Decline politely; offer to meet once payment shows

explanation.whatHappened: You offered to reschedule handover once funds actually credit.
explanation.why: Legitimate buyers understand bank delays and are willing to wait.

choices.label: Decline, block and report buyer on the marketplace

explanation.whatHappened: You identified deliberate fraud and reported the account.
explanation.why: Reporting fraudulent accounts helps safeguard fellow campus students.

messageOrEvent.text: The buyer walked away with your calculator, and no payment ever arrived.

outcome.title: Calculator Handed Over Without Payment
outcome.text: In this simulation, that choice would have cost you ₹1,800. The buyer took the item and the transaction never existed. No real money moved.

messageOrEvent.text: You safely held onto your calculator until verified payment.

outcome.title: Item Protected — Awaiting Real Credit
outcome.text: You refused to release the calculator without verified funds in your account. The buyer left and no fake transaction tricked you.

outcome.title: Scammer Blocked and Reported
outcome.text: You identified the fake payment screenshot ruse, safeguarded your property, and flagged the fraudulent buyer to protect other students.

recommendedSafeActions: Always check your personal bank balance directly in your app before handing over goods
Never accept payment screenshots as confirmation of received money
Do not let artificial time pressure rush your security verification routines
learningSummary: A screenshot is merely an image file that can be easily forged or manipulated. Always verify the incoming credit directly in your personal bank or UPI statement.
